summary: Juichiro Tanabe studied as a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford (2000-2001) and studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

Specializing in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies, Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire studied at Bourbon College and Lycée Louis-le-Grand. He served as Professor of Greek at the Collège de France (1838-1852).

Jules Bloch studied at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet. An Indologist and linguist, he held posts at INALCO (1921-1937), EPHE (1919-1951), and the Collège de France (1936-1951).

Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar Jules Brooks Levinson completed his PhD at the University of Virginia in 1994 under Jeffrey Hopkins. He also studied under multiple traditional teachers and taught religion at Hamline University (attested 1996).

Historian Jules Michelet studied at Lycée Charlemagne before teaching at the École Normale Supérieure from 1827. He later served as section chief at the Archives nationales (1831-1852) and Professor of History at the Collège de France (1838-1852).

Jules Oppert was a linguist and historian who earned his PhD from Kiel University (1847) after studies at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Berlin. He taught at INALCO (1857) and was a professor at the Collège de France (1874-1905).

Julia A. B. Hegewald is an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied at SOAS (BA ~1991-1994, PhD ~1994-1998) and the University of Oxford (MA ~1994-1998), later completing her Habilitation at RWTH Aachen University (~1999-2008).

Julia Ching studied at the College of New Rochelle, Catholic University of America, and Australian National University (PhD ~1968-1971). Active in Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies, she became a professor at the University of Toronto in 1978.

Working in Sinology and art history/archaeology, Julia F. Andrews studied at Brown University, Harvard University, and the University of California, Berkeley. She joined the faculty at Ohio State University around 1987.
Julia Leslie worked in the fields of Indology and religious studies, and held a post at SOAS University of London from around 1993 to 2004.

Julian Schott works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. His attested academic posts include research fellow at the University of Hamburg (2026) and faculty member at the University of Vienna (2026).

Julian Strube, a scholar of religious studies and Indology, habilitated at Heidelberg University. He taught at Vienna (2021-2024) before being appointed professor of religious studies and intercultural theology at the University of Göttingen in 2024.

Juliane Schober, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, earned her PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989. She later held posts as Associate Professor (attested 2007) and Professor (attested 1997) at Arizona State University.

Julie A. Gifford, a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies, earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Frank E. Reynolds. She held an attested post at Miami University in 2011.

Julius Eggeling studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber at Breslau and Berlin. He taught Sanskrit at University College London (1872-1875) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (1875-1914).

Julius Euting studied at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Ernst Heinrich Meier. A linguist and historian, he served as honorary professor at the University of Strasbourg (1880) and director of its library (1900-1909).

Julius Grill studied at the University of Tübingen and under Rudolf von Roth, earning a licentiate from Jena. A scholar of Indology and religious studies, he was Professor of Old Testament Exegesis at Tübingen (1888-1913).

Julius Jolly studied under Albrecht Weber and Martin Haug at Munich, Berlin, and Leipzig, habilitating at Würzburg. An Indologist and linguist, he was a long-time professor at the University of Würzburg (1877-1920).

Julius Lipner studied under Hywel David Lewis at King's College London, as well as at Jadavpur and Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth. He served as Professor of Hinduism and the Comparative Study of Religion at the University of Cambridge (1975-2013).

Julius Mohl studied at Tübingen and under Silvestre de Sacy and Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat in Paris. A scholar of Sinology and Iranian studies, he held professorships at the University of Tübingen (1826-1834) and the Collège de France (1847-1876).
